name: Subconscious: the person's own knowledge, admitted to the working stream by the goal
description: Draws on what the person's own material holds (their cards, files, notes, past conversations and recalled context) and decides at every step what of it enters the working stream, by whether it bears on the request's goal condition, with the scope fence applied once at that gate.
purpose: Keeps each request's working stream holding the part of the person's own knowledge its goal needs, so a fast model is neither misled by near misses nor buried in noise.
approach: Judges each candidate from the person's material against the request's goal condition and scope before it enters the working stream, settling clear cases cheaply and asking a small model only on the borderline.
out_of_scope: Finding the candidates (retrieval, card selection and reading keep their own specifications), and knowledge about the world beyond the person's own material.
milestones: 1. A labelled set of steps exists, each with candidate items marked needed, irrelevant, near miss or out of scope, and recency_window has a recorded result on it. 2. A goal-conditioned implementation admits more needed items than recency_window at the same or better precision, with no out-of-scope item admitted.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-28 for the specification owner to confirm. The specification owner's design: the subconscious is the person's own knowledge and context; it does context assembly and tool calls and checks which context is worth showing to the mind. Assembly and reading are already specified (select-context, gather-evidence, search-cards-and-specs, recall-recent-context); this solution adds only the admission check, which no existing record owns. Today cards are filtered once at the start (core/card_filter.py) and observations are admitted by recency (core/planner_context.py). Its value grows with a carried stream, where an admitted item stays for every later step. On cheap-model routing a reviewer handed a decision argued with correct decisions while the same model asked one question of fact did well, so the borderline judge asks whether an item bears on the goal, never whether the plan is right. The specification owner's direction (2026-10-28): intuition is conceptually part of the subconscious. Recorded as outcome_precedents: at admission, past requests like this one and how they ended are surfaced to the working stream as a hint, never as a decision; the outcome history is kept by the long view (hold-the-intents). The anticipation engine predicts the next ask and recipes replay past successes; neither learns from how a turn ended, so this is new.
measures_of_success: Needed items are admitted, irrelevant and near-miss items are kept out, and no out-of-scope item is ever admitted, at no more than one small model call per step. Standing conditions: Apply the scope fence at the gate on every path. Treat an empty or near-miss lookup as not found.
parameters: Thresholds per source, the borderline band that calls the judge, the judge's tier, and the per-step token budget.
inputs: The goal condition, the turn's scope tags, and candidate items with their source and scores.
outputs: The admitted items with a one-line reason each, and the dropped ones with theirs, for the explanation of how an answer was reached.
effects: At most one small model call per step for borderline items; no writes.
usage_notes: Sits between retrieval and the working stream. Selected today: recency_window.

name: Justified model calls
description: Keeps every model call tied to a registered prompt spec with an owner solution and metric, so a call stays only while its measured value outweighs its cost and time.
purpose: Gives an operator a known value, cost and time for every model call, so spend and latency go only to prompts that earn them and a cheaper or faster option is not missed.
approach: Every prompt is a registered PromptSpec (id, owner solution, metric, tier, cache layer, output schema, no-em-dash rule) in core/prompt_specs.py. One enforced call path, checked by tests/test_prompt_specs.py with a shrinking baseline, admits only registered prompts. A per-call ablation drops or downgrades the call and checks the owner metric.
out_of_scope: Choosing the model tier for a turn (choose-a-model-tier), the daily budget (track-usage-and-cost), and the content of any one prompt.
milestones: 1. Every call site is a registered spec and the baseline of unregistered sites is empty. 2. Each spec has a per-call ablation row on production-shaped cases. 3. Each spec has a budget for cost, tokens and latency set from the value its owner metric shows.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: dictated by Joshua 2026-10-28 and recorded as given, to be confirmed by him; not built beyond the registry and the enforcement test, so the metric is unmeasured. Known today: the call sites still unregistered are listed in tests/prompt_spec_baseline.txt; spend-weighted value not computed.
measures_of_success: The metric is read from recorded rows without invented readings. Standing conditions: Never invent a reading. Label rows taken from eval traces until production data exists.
parameters: The bar (0.8) and each prompt's own budget for cost, tokens and latency.
inputs: The per-call usage records tagged with the spec id (quest_ai_runner/usage.py) and production-shaped eval cases (quest_ai_prod_examples shapes).
outputs: A per-prompt table and the share of average model spend that is justified.
effects: No model call of its own except the ablation runs, which are paid and run only by decision with a budget.
usage_notes: Selected today: spec_registry. The ablation arm is proposed and not built.
